questions.stem: What do we learn about gazpacho?

options.A: It is a typical salad.
options.B: It is a Spanish soup.
options.C: It is a weird vegetable.
options.D: It is a kind of spicy food.

questions.cn: 关于西班牙冷汤，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.B: 它是西班牙的一种汤。
optionsCn.C: 它是一种奇怪的蔬菜。
optionsCn.D: 它是一种辛辣食物。

questions.stem: For what purpose is stale bread mixed into gazpacho?

options.A: To make it thicker.
options.B: To make it more nutritious.
options.C: To add to its appeal.
options.D: To replace an ingredient.

questions.cn: 把放陈的面包拌进冷汤里是为了什么？

optionsCn.B: 让它更有营养。
optionsCn.C: 增加它的吸引力。
optionsCn.D: 替代一种配料。

questions.stem: Why does the woman think gazpacho is healthy?

options.A: It contains very little fat.
options.B: It uses olive oil in cooking.
options.C: It uses no artificial additives.
options.D: It is mainly made of vegetables.

questions.cn: 女士为什么认为西班牙冷汤是健康的？

optionsCn.B: 它烹饪时使用橄榄油。
optionsCn.C: 它不使用人工添加剂。
optionsCn.D: 它主要由蔬菜制成。

questions.stem: What does the woman say about cured ham?

options.A: It does not go stale for two years.
options.B: It takes no special skill to prepare.
options.C: It comes from a special kind of pig.
options.D: It is a delicacy blended with bread.

questions.cn: 关于腌火腿，女士说了什么？

optionsCn.B: 制作它不需要特殊技巧。
optionsCn.C: 它来自一种特殊的猪。
optionsCn.D: 它是与面包混合的美味。

lines.t: Conversation 1.
lines.cn: 对话一。

lines.t: M: What's all that?
lines.cn: M：这些是什么呀？

lines.t: M: Are you going to make a salad?
lines.cn: M：你要做沙拉吗？

lines.t: F: No, I'm going to make a gazpacho.
lines.cn: F：不，我要做西班牙冷汤。

lines.t: M: What's that?
lines.cn: M：那是什么？

lines.t: F: Gazpacho is a cold soup from Spain.
lines.cn: F：西班牙冷汤是西班牙的一种凉汤。

lines.t: F: It's mostly vegetables.
lines.cn: F：主要原料是蔬菜。

lines.t: F: I guess you could call it a liquid salad.
lines.cn: F：可以说它是一种液态沙拉吧。

lines.t: M: Cold soup?
lines.cn: M：凉汤？

lines.t: M: Sounds weird.
lines.cn: M：听起来挺奇怪。

lines.t: F: It's delicious, trust me.
lines.cn: F：相信我，味道很好。

lines.t: F: I tried it for the first time during my summer vacation in Spain.
lines.cn: F：我第一次喝是在西班牙过暑假的时候。

lines.t: F: You see, in the south of Spain, it gets very hot in the summer, up to 40 degrees Celsius.
lines.cn: F：你知道，西班牙南部夏天非常热，气温能到 40 摄氏度。

lines.t: F: So a cold gazpacho is very refreshing.
lines.cn: F：所以冰凉的冷汤非常解暑。

lines.t: F: The main ingredients are tomato, cucumber, bell peppers, olive oil and stale bread.
lines.cn: F：主要配料是番茄、黄瓜、甜椒、橄榄油和放陈了的面包。

lines.t: M: Stale bread?
lines.cn: M：放陈的面包？

lines.t: M: Surely you mean bread for dipping into the soup.
lines.cn: M：你肯定是指用来蘸汤的面包吧。

lines.t: F: No, bread is crushed and blended in like everything else.
lines.cn: F：不是，面包要像其他所有食材一样碾碎后搅进去。

lines.t: F: It adds texture and thickness to the soup.
lines.cn: F：它给汤增加口感和浓稠度。

lines.t: M: Hmm.
lines.cn: M：嗯。

lines.t: M: And is it healthy?
lines.cn: M：那它健康吗？

lines.t: F: Sure.
lines.cn: F：当然。

lines.t: F: As I said earlier, it's mostly vegetables.
lines.cn: F：就像我刚才说的，它主要是蔬菜。

lines.t: F: You can also add different things if you like, such as hard-boiled egg or cured ham.
lines.cn: F：如果喜欢，你还可以加些别的东西，比如煮熟的鸡蛋或腌火腿。

lines.t: M: Cured ham?
lines.cn: M：腌火腿？

lines.t: M: What's that?
lines.cn: M：那是什么？

lines.t: F: That's another Spanish delicacy.
lines.cn: F：那是另一种西班牙美味。

lines.t: F: Have you never heard of it?
lines.cn: F：你从没听说过吗？

lines.t: F: It's quite famous.
lines.cn: F：它相当有名。

lines.t: M: No.
lines.cn: M：没有。

lines.t: M: Is it good, too?
lines.cn: M：它也好吃吗？

lines.t: F: Oh, yeah, definitely.
lines.cn: F：哦，那当然。

lines.t: F: It's amazing.
lines.cn: F：非常棒。

lines.t: F: It's a little dry and salty and it's very expensive because it comes from a special type of pig that only eats a special type of food.
lines.cn: F：它有点干、有点咸，而且非常贵，因为它来自一种只吃特殊饲料的特殊猪种。

lines.t: F: The ham is covered in salt to dry and preserve it and left to hang for up to two years.
lines.cn: F：这种火腿用盐包裹来风干保存，然后悬挂起来长达两年。

lines.t: F: It has a very distinct flavour.
lines.cn: F：它的风味非常独特。

lines.t: M: Hmm.
lines.cn: M：嗯。

lines.t: M: Sounds interesting.
lines.cn: M：听起来挺有意思。

lines.t: M: Where can I find some?
lines.cn: M：我在哪儿能买到？

lines.t: F: It used to be difficult to get Spanish produce here, but it's now a lot more common.
lines.cn: F：以前在这里很难买到西班牙食品，但现在常见多了。

lines.t: F: Most large supermarket chains have cured ham in little packets, but in Spain you can buy a whole leg.
lines.cn: F：大多数大型连锁超市都有小包装的腌火腿，而在西班牙你可以买整条腿。

lines.t: M: A whole pig leg?
lines.cn: M：整条猪腿？

lines.t: M: Why would anybody want so much ham?
lines.cn: M：怎么会有人想要这么多火腿？

lines.t: F: In Spain, many people buy a whole leg for special group events such as Christmas.
lines.cn: F：在西班牙，很多人为了圣诞节这类群体聚会会买整条腿。

lines.t: F: They cut it themselves into very thin slices with a long flat knife.
lines.cn: F：他们用一把长而扁的刀自己把它切成很薄的片。

tasks.title: Sec A · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the woman think of table wines?

options.A: They come in a great variety.
options.B: They do not make decent gifts.
options.C: They do not vary much in price.
options.D: They go well with Italian food.

questions.cn: 女士怎么看餐酒？

optionsCn.B: 它们不适合作为像样的礼物。
optionsCn.C: 它们价格差别不大。
optionsCn.D: 它们与意大利菜很搭。

questions.stem: What is the price range of wine the man will consider?

options.D: Around $150.

questions.cn: 男士会考虑的价格区间是多少？

optionsCn.D: 150 美元左右。

questions.stem: Why does the woman recommend red wines?

options.A: They are a healthy choice for elderly people.
options.B: They are especially popular among Italians.
options.C: They symbolize good health and longevity.
options.D: They go well with different kinds of food.

questions.cn: 女士为什么推荐红葡萄酒？

optionsCn.A: 它们对老年人来说是健康的选择。
optionsCn.B: 它们在意大利人当中特别受欢迎。
optionsCn.C: 它们象征健康和长寿。
optionsCn.D: 它们能与不同种类的食物搭配。

questions.stem: What do we learn about the wine the man finally bought?

options.A: It is wine imported from California.
options.B: It is less spicy than all other red wines.
options.C: It is far more expensive than he expected.
options.D: It is Italy's most famous type of red wine.

questions.cn: 关于男士最终买的酒，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 它是从加州进口的葡萄酒。
optionsCn.B: 它比其他所有红葡萄酒都不那么辛辣。
optionsCn.C: 它比他预想的贵得多。
optionsCn.D: 它是意大利最有名的红葡萄酒类型。

lines.t: Conversation 2.
lines.cn: 对话二。

lines.t: M: Hello.
lines.cn: M：你好。

lines.t: M: I wish to buy a bottle of wine.
lines.cn: M：我想买一瓶葡萄酒。

lines.t: F: Hi.
lines.cn: F：你好。

lines.t: F: Yes.
lines.cn: F：好的。

lines.t: F: What kind of wine would you like?
lines.cn: F：您想要哪种葡萄酒？

lines.t: M: I don't know.
lines.cn: M：我不知道。

lines.t: M: Sorry.
lines.cn: M：抱歉。

lines.t: M: I don't know much about wine.
lines.cn: M：我对葡萄酒不太懂。

lines.t: F: That's no problem at all.
lines.cn: F：完全没问题。

lines.t: F: What's the occasion and how much would you like to spend?
lines.cn: F：是什么场合？您打算花多少钱？

lines.t: M: It's for my boss.
lines.cn: M：是送给我老板的。

lines.t: M: It's his birthday.
lines.cn: M：是他的生日。

lines.t: M: I know he likes wine, but I don't know what type.
lines.cn: M：我知道他喜欢葡萄酒，但不知道喜欢哪种。

lines.t: M: I also do not want anything too expensive.
lines.cn: M：我也不想要太贵的。

lines.t: M: Maybe mid-range.
lines.cn: M：中等价位吧。

lines.t: M: How much would you say is a mid-range bottle of wine, approximately?
lines.cn: M：您说一瓶中等价位的葡萄酒大概多少钱？

lines.t: F: Well, it varies greatly.
lines.cn: F：嗯，差别很大。

lines.t: F: Our lowest prices are around $6 a bottle, but those are table wines.
lines.cn: F：我们最低价大约每瓶 6 美元，但那些是餐酒。

lines.t: F: They are not very special, and I would not suggest them as a gift.
lines.cn: F：它们不太特别，我不建议用作礼物。

lines.t: F: On the other end, our most expensive bottles are over $150.
lines.cn: F：另一头，我们最贵的酒超过 150 美元。

lines.t: F: If you are looking for something priced in the middle, I would say anything between $30 and $60 would make a decent gift.
lines.cn: F：如果您想找中间价位的，我认为 30 到 60 美元之间的都可以作为不错的礼物。

lines.t: F: How does that sound?
lines.cn: F：您觉得怎么样？

lines.t: M: Hmm.
lines.cn: M：嗯。

lines.t: M: Yeah.
lines.cn: M：好。

lines.t: M: I guess something in the vicinity of $30 or $40 would be good.
lines.cn: M：我想 30 或 40 美元左右的应该不错。

lines.t: M: Which type would you recommend?
lines.cn: M：您推荐哪一种？

lines.t: F: I would say the safest option is always a red wine.
lines.cn: F：我认为最稳妥的选择永远是红葡萄酒。

lines.t: F: They are generally more popular than whites and can usually be paired with food more easily.
lines.cn: F：它们通常比白葡萄酒更受欢迎，也更容易与食物搭配。

lines.t: F: Our specialty here are Italian wines, and these tend to be fruity with medium acidity.
lines.cn: F：我们这里的特色是意大利葡萄酒，它们往往果香浓郁、酸度适中。

lines.t: F: This one here is a Chianti, which is perhaps Italy's most famous type of red wine.
lines.cn: F：这一款是基安蒂，大概是意大利最有名的红葡萄酒类型。

lines.t: F: Alternatively, you may wish to try and surprise your boss with something less common, such as this Zinfandel.
lines.cn: F：或者，您也可以试试用不那么常见的酒给老板一个惊喜，比如这款仙粉黛。

lines.t: F: The grapes are originally native to Croatia, but this winery is in eastern Italy, and it has a more spicy and peppery flavour.
lines.cn: F：这种葡萄原产于克罗地亚，但这家酒庄位于意大利东部，它的风味更辛辣、更具胡椒味。

lines.t: F: So, to summarise, the Chianti is more classical, and the Zinfandel more exciting.
lines.cn: F：总而言之，基安蒂更经典，仙粉黛更有惊喜。

lines.t: F: Both are similarly priced at just under $40.
lines.cn: F：两者价格相近，都在 40 美元略低一点。

lines.t: M: I will go with Chianti then.
lines.cn: M：那我就选基安蒂吧。

lines.t: M: Thanks.
lines.cn: M：谢谢。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say many people enjoy doing?

options.A: Learning others' secrets.
options.B: Searching for information.
options.C: Decoding secret messages.
options.D: Spreading sensational news.

questions.cn: 讲话者说许多人喜欢做什么？

optionsCn.B: 搜寻信息。
optionsCn.C: 破译秘密信息。
optionsCn.D: 传播耸人听闻的消息。

questions.stem: What do we learn about the Navajo Code Talkers?

options.A: They helped the U.S. army in World War II.
options.B: They could write down spoken codes promptly.
options.C: They were assigned to decode enemy messages.
options.D: They were good at breaking enemy secret codes.

questions.cn: 关于纳瓦霍密码译员，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们在二战中帮助过美国军队。
optionsCn.B: 他们能迅速记下口头密码。
optionsCn.C: 他们被派去破译敌方信息。
optionsCn.D: 他们擅长破解敌方密码。

questions.stem: What is the speaker mainly talking about?

options.A: Important battles fought in the Pacific War.
options.B: Decoding of secret messages in war times.
options.C: A military code that was never broken.
options.D: Navajo Indians' contribution to code breaking.

questions.cn: 讲话者主要在谈什么？

optionsCn.A: 太平洋战争中的重要战役。
optionsCn.B: 战时秘密信息的破译。
optionsCn.C: 一种从未被破译的军事密码。
optionsCn.D: 纳瓦霍印第安人对破译密码的贡献。

lines.t: Passage 1.
lines.cn: 短文一。

lines.t: Many people enjoy secret codes.
lines.cn: 许多人喜欢密码。

lines.t: The harder the code, the more some people will try to figure it out.
lines.cn: 密码越难，就越有人想要破解它。

lines.t: In wartime, codes are especially important.
lines.cn: 战时，密码尤为重要。

lines.t: They help armies send news about battles and the size of enemy forces.
lines.cn: 它们帮助军队传递关于战斗和敌军规模的消息。

lines.t: Neither side wants its code broken by the other.
lines.cn: 双方都不希望自己的密码被对方破译。

lines.t: One very important code was never broken.
lines.cn: 有一种非常重要的密码从未被破译。

lines.t: It was used during World War II by the Americans.
lines.cn: 二战期间美国人曾使用它。

lines.t: It was a spoken code, never written down.
lines.cn: 这是一种口头密码，从不写下来。

lines.t: And it was developed and used by Navajo Indians.
lines.cn: 它由纳瓦霍印第安人发明并使用。

lines.t: They were called the Navajo Code Talkers.
lines.cn: 他们被称为纳瓦霍密码译员。

lines.t: The Navajos created the code in their own language.
lines.cn: 纳瓦霍人用自己的语言创造了这套密码。

lines.t: Navajo is hard to learn, and only a few people know it.
lines.cn: 纳瓦霍语很难学，只有少数人懂。

lines.t: So it was pretty certain that the enemy would not be able to understand the Code Talkers.
lines.cn: 所以几乎可以肯定，敌人无法听懂这些密码译员的话。

lines.t: In addition, the Talkers used code words.
lines.cn: 此外，这些译员还使用代号。

lines.t: They called a submarine an iron fish, and a small bomb thrown by hand a potato.
lines.cn: 他们把潜艇称作“铁鱼”，把手投的小型炸弹称作“土豆”。

lines.t: If they wanted to spell something, they used code words for letters of the alphabet.
lines.cn: 如果要拼写某个词，他们就用代表字母表字母的代号。

lines.t: For instance, the letter A was ant or apple or axe.
lines.cn: 比如，字母 A 对应的是蚂蚁、苹果或斧头。

lines.t: The Code Talkers worked mostly in the islands in the Pacific.
lines.cn: 密码译员主要活跃在太平洋诸岛上。

lines.t: One or two would be assigned to a group of soldiers.
lines.cn: 一两名译员会被分配到一支士兵队伍中。

lines.t: They would send messages by field telephone to the Code Talker in the next group.
lines.cn: 他们用野战电话把消息传给下一支部队里的密码译员。

lines.t: And he would relay the information to his commander.
lines.cn: 再由他把信息转达给自己的指挥官。

lines.t: The Code Talkers played an important part in several battles.
lines.cn: 密码译员在好几场战役中都发挥了重要作用。

lines.t: They helped troops coordinate their movements and attacks.
lines.cn: 他们帮助部队协调行动和进攻。

lines.t: After the war, the U.
lines.cn: 战争结束后，美国

lines.t: S.
lines.cn: 政府

lines.t: government honored them for what they had accomplished.
lines.cn: 表彰了他们所立下的功绩。

lines.t: Theirs was the most successful wartime code ever used.
lines.cn: 他们的密码是有史以来使用过的最成功的战时密码。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say will happen in the next 20 years?

options.A: All services will be personalized.
options.B: A lot of knowledge-intensive jobs will be replaced.
options.C: Technology will revolutionize all sectors of industry.
options.D: More information will be available.

questions.cn: 讲话者说未来 20 年会发生什么？

optionsCn.B: 许多知识密集型工作将被取代。
optionsCn.C: 技术将使所有工业部门发生革命性变化。
optionsCn.D: 会有更多信息可供获取。

questions.stem: Where will young people have more chances to find jobs?

options.A: In the robotics industry.
options.B: In the information service.
options.C: In the personal care sector.
options.D: In high-end manufacturing.

questions.cn: 年轻人将在哪里更有机会找到工作？

optionsCn.B: 在信息服务领域。
optionsCn.C: 在个人护理部门。
optionsCn.D: 在高端制造业。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about therapists?

options.A: They charge high prices.
options.B: They need lots of training.
options.C: They cater to the needs of young people.
options.D: They focus on customers' specific needs.

questions.cn: 关于治疗师，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.B: 他们需要大量培训。
optionsCn.C: 他们满足年轻人的需求。
optionsCn.D: 他们专注于顾客的具体需求。

questions.stem: What is the speaker's book about? This is the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1, with a single line through the center.

options.A: The rising demand in education and healthcare in the next 20 years.
options.B: The disruption caused by technology in traditionally well-paid jobs.
options.C: The tremendous changes new technology will bring to people's lives.
options.D: The amazing amount of personal attention people would like to have.

questions.cn: 讲话者的书是关于什么的？

optionsCn.A: 未来 20 年教育和医疗需求的上升。
optionsCn.B: 技术对传统高薪工作造成的冲击。
optionsCn.C: 新技术将给人们生活带来的巨大变化。
optionsCn.D: 人们希望获得的大量个人关照。

lines.t: Passage 2.
lines.cn: 短文二。

lines.t: If you are young and thinking about your career, you'll want to know where you can make a living.
lines.cn: 如果你还年轻，正在考虑自己的职业，你会想知道在哪里能谋生。

lines.t: Well, there's going to be a technological replacement of a lot of knowledge-intensive jobs in the next 20 years, particularly in the two largest sectors of the labor force with professional skills.
lines.cn: 在未来 20 年里，许多知识密集型工作将被技术取代，尤其是在劳动力中拥有专业技能的两大部门。

lines.t: One is teaching, and the other, health care.
lines.cn: 一个是教育，另一个是医疗保健。

lines.t: You have so many applications and software and platforms that are going to come in and provide information and service in these two fields.
lines.cn: 会有许许多多的应用、软件和平台进入这两个领域，提供信息和服务。

lines.t: Which means a lot of health care and education sectors will be radically changed, and a lot of jobs will be lost.
lines.cn: 这意味着医疗和教育部门会发生根本性变化，许多工作岗位将消失。

lines.t: Now, where will the new jobs be found?
lines.cn: 那么，新的工作机会会在哪里出现？

lines.t: Well, the one sector of the economy that can't be easily duplicated by even smart technologies is the caring sector, the personal care sector.
lines.cn: 嗯，经济中唯一无法被哪怕最聪明的技术轻易复制的一个部门，就是照护部门，即个人护理部门。

lines.t: That is, you can't really get a robot to do a great massage or physical therapy, or you can't get the kind of personal attention you need with regard to therapy or any other personal service.
lines.cn: 也就是说，你没法让机器人做一次出色的按摩或理疗，也没法在治疗或其他个人服务中获得你所需要的那种周到关照。

lines.t: There could be very high-end personal services.
lines.cn: 可能会有非常高端的个人服务。

lines.t: Therapists do charge a lot of money.
lines.cn: 治疗师确实收费很高。

lines.t: I think there's no limit to the amount of personal attention and personal care people would like if they could afford it.
lines.cn: 我认为，只要负担得起，人们想要的个人关照和护理是没有上限的。

lines.t: But the real question in the future is, how can people afford these things if they don't have money, because they can't get a job that pays enough?
lines.cn: 但未来真正的问题是：如果人们没有钱，因为他们找不到薪水足够的工作，他们又怎么负担得起这些？

lines.t: That's why I wrote this book, which is about how to reorganize the economy for the future when technology brings about disruptive changes to what we used to consider high-income work.
lines.cn: 这正是我写这本书的原因，它讲的是当技术给我们过去认为的高收入工作带来颠覆性变化时，如何为未来重组经济。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do we learn from the lecture about the world's oldest paved road in Egypt?

options.A: It was the longest road in ancient Egypt.
options.B: It was constructed some 500 years ago.
options.C: It lay 8 miles from the monument sites.
options.D: It linked a stone pit to some waterways.

questions.cn: 关于埃及那条世界上最古老的铺砌道路，我们从讲座中了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 它是古埃及最长的道路。
optionsCn.B: 它建于约 500 年前。
optionsCn.C: 它距纪念性建筑工地 8 英里。
optionsCn.D: 它把一处采石场与一些水道连接起来。

questions.stem: What did the researchers discover in the stone pit?

options.A: Saws used for cutting stone.
options.B: Traces left by early explorers.
options.C: An ancient geographical map.
options.D: Some stone tool segments.

questions.cn: 研究人员在采石场发现了什么？

optionsCn.B: 早期探险者留下的痕迹。
optionsCn.C: 一幅古代地图。
optionsCn.D: 一些石制工具的残段。

questions.stem: For what purpose was the paved road built?

options.A: To transport stones to block floods.
options.B: To provide services for the stone pit.
options.C: To link the various monument sites.
options.D: To connect the villages along the Nile.

questions.cn: 这条铺砌道路是为着什么目的修建的？

optionsCn.B: 为采石场提供服务。
optionsCn.C: 连接各个纪念性建筑工地。
optionsCn.D: 连接尼罗河沿岸的村庄。

lines.t: Recording 1.
lines.cn: 录音一。

lines.t: American researchers have discovered the world's oldest paved road, a 4,600-year-old highway.
lines.cn: 美国研究人员发现了世界上最古老的铺砌道路，一条有 4600 年历史的公路。

lines.t: It linked a stone pit in the Egyptian desert to waterways that carried blocks to monument sites along the Nile.
lines.cn: 它把埃及沙漠中的一处采石场与水道连接起来，水道再把石块运往尼罗河沿岸的纪念性建筑工地。

lines.t: The eight-mile road is at least 500 years older than any previously discovered road.
lines.cn: 这条 8 英里长的道路至少比此前发现的任何道路都早 500 年。

lines.t: It is the only paved road discovered in ancient Egypt, said geologist Thomas Bowne of the United States Geological Survey.
lines.cn: 美国地质调查局的地质学家托马斯·鲍恩说，这是古埃及唯一被发现的铺砌道路。

lines.t: He reported the discovery on Friday.
lines.cn: 他在周五报告了这一发现。

lines.t: The road probably doesn't rank with the pyramids as a construction feat, but it is a major engineering achievement, said his colleague, geologist James Harrell of the University of Toledo.
lines.cn: 他的同事、托莱多大学地质学家詹姆斯·哈雷尔说，这条路或许无法与金字塔相提并论，但它是一项重大的工程成就。

lines.t: Not only is the road earlier than we thought possible, we didn't even think they built roads.
lines.cn: 这条路不仅早于我们以为可能的年代，我们甚至根本没想过他们会修路。

lines.t: The researchers also made a discovery in the stone pit at the northern end of the road, the first evidence that the Egyptians used rock saws.
lines.cn: 研究人员还在道路北端的采石场有了一项发现：这是埃及人使用石锯的首个证据。

lines.t: This is the oldest example of saws being used for cutting stone, said Bowne's colleague James Hoffmeyer of Wheaton College in Illinois.
lines.cn: 鲍恩的同事、伊利诺伊州惠顿学院的詹姆斯·霍夫迈耶说，这是用锯切割石头的最古老实例。

lines.t: That's two technologies we didn't know they had, Harrell said.
lines.cn: 哈雷尔说，这是我们原先不知道他们掌握的两项技术。

lines.t: And we don't know why they were both abandoned.
lines.cn: 而且我们不知道这两项技术为何都被弃用了。

lines.t: The road was discovered in the Fayum Depression, about 45 miles southwest of Cairo.
lines.cn: 这条路是在开罗西南约 45 英里的法尤姆洼地被发现的。

lines.t: Short segments of the road had been observed by earlier explorers, Bowne said, but they failed to realise its significance or follow up on their observations.
lines.cn: 鲍恩说，早期的探险者曾看到过这条路的一些短小路段，但他们没能意识到它的重要性，也没有进一步追踪自己的观察。

lines.t: Bowne and his colleague stumbled across it while they were doing geological mapping in the region.
lines.cn: 鲍恩和同事是在该地区进行地质测绘时偶然发现它的。

lines.t: The road was clearly built to provide services for the newly discovered stone pit.
lines.cn: 这条路显然是为新发现的采石场提供运输服务而修建的。

lines.t: Bowne and Harrell have found the camp that housed workers at the stone pit.
lines.cn: 鲍恩和哈雷尔已经找到了当年采石场工人居住的营地。

lines.t: The road appears today to go nowhere, ending in the middle of the desert.
lines.cn: 如今这条路看起来毫无去处，消失在沙漠中央。

lines.t: When it was built, its terminal was a dock on the shore of Lake Moiris, which had an elevation of about 66 feet above sea level, the same as the dock.
lines.cn: 在它建成时，其终点是莫伊里斯湖畔的一个码头，湖面海拔约 66 英尺，与码头齐平。

lines.t: Lake Moiris received its water from the annual floods of the Nile.
lines.cn: 莫伊里斯湖的水来自尼罗河每年的泛滥。

lines.t: At the time of the floods, the river and lake were at the same level and connected through a gap in the hills, near the modern villages of El Lajun and Hawara.
lines.cn: 洪水期间，河与湖水位相同，并通过山间的一个缺口相连，那里靠近今天的拉洪村和哈瓦拉村。

lines.t: Harrell and Bowne believe that blocks were loaded onto barges during the dry season, then floated over to the Nile during the floods to be shipped off to the monument sites at Giza and Saqqara.
lines.cn: 哈雷尔和鲍恩认为，石块在旱季被装上驳船，洪水期再漂运到尼罗河，然后运往吉萨和萨卡拉的纪念性建筑工地。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 2 组

questions.stem: What does the speaker find especially strange?

options.A: Dr. Gong didn't give him any conventional tests.
options.B: Dr. Gong marked his office with a hand-painted sign.
options.C: Dr. Gong didn't ask him any questions about his pain.
options.D: Dr. Gong slipped in needles where he felt no pain.

questions.cn: 讲话者觉得特别奇怪的是什么？

optionsCn.A: 龚医生没给他做任何常规检查。
optionsCn.B: 龚医生用一块手写招牌标示自己的诊所。
optionsCn.C: 龚医生没有问他任何关于疼痛的问题。
optionsCn.D: 龚医生把针扎在他不觉得疼的地方。

questions.stem: Why did the speaker go see Dr. Gong?

options.A: He had heard of the wonders acupuncture could work.
options.B: Dr. Gong was very famous in New York's Chinatown.
options.C: Previous medical treatments failed to relieve his pain.
options.D: He found the expensive medical tests unaffordable.

questions.cn: 讲话者为什么去找龚医生？

optionsCn.A: 他听说过针灸能有奇效。
optionsCn.B: 龚医生在纽约唐人街非常有名。
optionsCn.C: 先前的治疗未能缓解他的疼痛。
optionsCn.D: 他觉得那些昂贵的检查负担不起。

questions.stem: What accounts for the growing popularity of acupuncture in the United States, according to the speaker?

options.A: More and more patients ask for the treatment.
options.B: Acupuncture techniques have been perfected.
options.C: It doesn't need the conventional medical tests.
options.D: It does not have any negative side effects.

questions.cn: 根据讲话者，针灸在美国越来越受欢迎的原因是什么？

optionsCn.A: 越来越多的病人要求接受这种治疗。
optionsCn.B: 针灸技术已被完善。
optionsCn.C: 它不需要常规医学检查。
optionsCn.D: 它没有任何副作用。

lines.t: Recording 2.
lines.cn: 录音二。

lines.t: The thin, extremely sharp needles didn't hurt at all going in.
lines.cn: 那些又细又极锋利的针扎进去时一点也不疼。

lines.t: Dr.
lines.cn: 龚

lines.t: Gong pierced them into my left arm, around the elbow that had been bothering me.
lines.cn: 医生把它们扎进我的左臂，扎在一直让我难受的肘部周围。

lines.t: Other needles were slipped into my left wrist and, strangely, into my right arm, and then into both my closed eyelids.
lines.cn: 其他针则刺入我的左手腕，奇怪的是，还刺入我的右臂，然后扎进我两只闭着的眼皮。

lines.t: There wasn't any discomfort, just a mild warming sensation.
lines.cn: 没有任何不适，只有一种微微发热的感觉。

lines.t: However, I did begin to wonder what had driven me here.
lines.cn: 不过，我开始想，究竟是什么把我带到了这里。

lines.t: To the office of Dr.
lines.cn: 来到纽约唐人街的

lines.t: James Gong in New York's Chinatown.
lines.cn: 詹姆斯·龚医生的诊室。

lines.t: Then I remembered the torturing pain in that left elbow.
lines.cn: 然后我想起了左肘那折磨人的疼痛。

lines.t: Several trips to a hospital and two expensive, uncomfortable medical tests had failed to produce even a diagnosis.
lines.cn: 跑了好几趟医院，做了两项既昂贵又难受的医学检查，却连个诊断都没得出。

lines.t: Maybe you lean on your left arm too much, the doctor concluded, suggesting I see a bone doctor.
lines.cn: 医生得出结论说，也许是你左臂压得太多了，并建议我去看骨科医生。

lines.t: During the hours spent waiting in vain to see a bone doctor, I decided to take another track and try acupuncture.
lines.cn: 在白白等待看骨科医生的那些小时里，我决定换一条路，试试针灸。

lines.t: A Chinese-American friend recommended Dr.
lines.cn: 一位华裔美国朋友推荐了龚

lines.t: Gong.
lines.cn: 医生。

lines.t: I took the subway to Gong's second floor office, marked with a hand-painted sign.
lines.cn: 我坐地铁来到龚医生的诊所，它在二楼，挂着一块手写的招牌。

lines.t: Dr.
lines.cn: 龚

lines.t: Gong speaks English, but not often.
lines.cn: 医生会说英语，但不常说。

lines.t: Most of my questions to him were greeted with a friendly laugh, but I managed to let him know where my arm hurt.
lines.cn: 我问他的大部分问题都换来友好的笑声，但我总算让他知道了我手臂哪里疼。

lines.t: He asked me to go into a room, had me lie down on a bed, and went to work.
lines.cn: 他让我进一间屋子，让我躺到床上，然后开始动手。

lines.t: In the next room, I learned a woman dancer was also getting a treatment.
lines.cn: 我得知隔壁房间里有一位女舞者也在接受治疗。

lines.t: As I lay there a while, I drifted into a dreamlike state and fantasized about what she looked like.
lines.cn: 我躺着躺了一会儿，渐渐进入梦幻般的状态，开始想象她的模样。

lines.t: Acupuncturists today are as likely to be found on Park Avenue as on Mott Street.
lines.cn: 今天，针灸师在帕克大道和在莫特街上一样容易找到。

lines.t: In all, there are an estimated 10,000 acupuncturists in the country.
lines.cn: 全美估计共有一万名针灸师。

lines.t: Nowadays, a lot of medical doctors have learned acupuncture techniques.
lines.cn: 如今，许多医生都学会了针灸技术。

lines.t: So have a number of dentists.
lines.cn: 不少牙医也一样。

lines.t: Reason?
lines.cn: 原因呢？

lines.t: Patient demand.
lines.cn: 病人的需求。

lines.t: Few, though, can adequately explain how acupuncture works.
lines.cn: 不过，很少有人能充分解释针灸是如何起作用的。

lines.t: Acupuncturists may say that the body has more than 800 acupuncture points.
lines.cn: 针灸师可能会说，人体有 800 多个穴位。

lines.t: A life force called T circulates through the body.
lines.cn: 一种被称为“气”的生命力在体内循环。

lines.t: Points on the skin are energetically connected to specific organs, body structures, and systems.
lines.cn: 皮肤上的穴位与特定的器官、身体结构和系统在能量上相连接。

lines.t: Acupuncture points are stimulated to balance the circulation of T.
lines.cn: 刺激穴位是为了平衡“气”的运行。

lines.t: The truth is, though, acupuncture is at least 2,200 years old.
lines.cn: 但事实是，针灸至少有 2200 年的历史。

lines.t: Nobody really knows what's happening, says Paul Zmiewski, a Ph.
lines.cn: 保罗·兹米耶夫斯基说，其实没有人真正知道发生了什么，他是哲学

lines.t: D.
lines.cn: 博士，

lines.t: in Chinese Studies who practices acupuncture in Philadelphia.
lines.cn: 研究汉学，在费城从事针灸。

lines.t: After five treatments, there has been dramatic improvement in my arm, and the pain is a fraction of what it was.
lines.cn: 经过五次治疗后，我的手臂有了显著好转，疼痛只剩原来的一小部分。

lines.t: The mainly silent Dr.
lines.cn: 一直话不多的龚

lines.t: Gong finally even offered a diagnosis for what troubled me.
lines.cn: 医生最后甚至对我的病症给出了诊断。

lines.t: Pinched nerve, he said.
lines.cn: 他说，是神经受压迫。

lines.t: There is a growing popularity of acupuncture in the United States, according to the speaker.
lines.cn: 据讲话者说，针灸在美国越来越受欢迎。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 3 组
tasks.context: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What is the most common birth order characteristic in marriage?

options.A: They were on the verge of breaking up.
options.B: They were compatible despite differences.
options.C: They quarreled a lot and never resolved their arguments.
options.D: They argued persistently about whether to have children.

questions.cn: 婚姻中最常见的出生顺序特征是什么？

optionsCn.B: 尽管有差异，他们依然合得来。
optionsCn.C: 他们经常争吵，争论从未得到解决。
optionsCn.D: 他们为要不要孩子争吵不休。

questions.stem: What do we learn about Ronald and Lois?

options.A: Neither of them has any brothers or sisters.
options.B: Neither of them won their parents' favor.
options.C: They weren't spoiled in their childhood.
options.D: They didn't like to be the apple of their parents' eyes.

questions.cn: 关于罗纳德和洛伊丝，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们两人都没有兄弟姐妹。
optionsCn.B: 他们两人都没有得到父母的宠爱。
optionsCn.C: 他们童年时没有被娇惯。
optionsCn.D: 他们不喜欢做父母的掌上明珠。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about the oldest child in a family?

options.A: They are usually good at making friends.
options.B: They tend to be adventurous and creative.
options.C: They are often content with what they have.
options.D: They tend to be self-assured and responsible.

questions.cn: 关于家中的长子或长女，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.B: 他们往往爱冒险、有创造力。
optionsCn.C: 他们常常满足于自己拥有的。
optionsCn.D: 他们往往自信且有责任心。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about the only children?

options.A: They enjoy making friends.
options.B: They tend to be well adjusted.
options.C: They are least likely to take initiative.
options.D: They usually have successful marriages.

questions.cn: 关于独生子女，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.B: 他们往往适应良好。
optionsCn.C: 他们最不主动。
optionsCn.D: 他们通常婚姻幸福。

lines.t: Recording 3.
lines.cn: 录音三。

lines.t: Ronald and Lois, married for two decades, consider themselves a happy couple, but in the early years of their marriage, both were disturbed by persistent arguments that seemed to fade away without ever being truly resolved.
lines.cn: 结婚二十年的罗纳德和洛伊丝自认为是幸福的一对，但在婚姻的头几年，两人都被反复出现的争吵困扰——那些争吵似乎总是不了了之，从未真正解决。

lines.t: They uncovered clues to what was going wrong by researching a fascinating subject, how birth order affects not only your personality, but also how compatible you are with your mate.
lines.cn: 他们通过研究一个引人入胜的课题——出生顺序如何不仅影响你的性格，也影响你与伴侣的契合度——找到了问题所在的线索。

lines.t: Ronald and Lois are only children, and onlys grow up accustomed to being the apple of their parents' eyes.
lines.cn: 罗纳德和洛伊丝都是独生子女，独生子女从小就习惯做父母的掌上明珠。

lines.t: Match two onlys, and you have partners who subconsciously expect each other to continue fulfilling this expectation, while neither has much experience in the giving end.
lines.cn: 两个独生子女配在一起，双方都会下意识地期待对方继续满足这种期待，而谁都没有多少付出的经验。

lines.t: Here's a list of common birth order characteristics, and some thoughts on the best, and worst, marital matches for each.
lines.cn: 下面列出常见的出生顺序特征，以及针对每种情况的最佳和最差婚姻搭配。

lines.t: The oldest tends to be self-assured, responsible, a high achiever, and relatively serious and reserved.
lines.cn: 老大往往自信、有责任心、成就突出，而且比较严肃内向。

lines.t: He may be slow to make friends, perhaps content with only one companion.
lines.cn: 他可能不善于交朋友，也许有一个伙伴就满足了。

lines.t: The best matches are with a youngest, an only, or a mate raised in a large family.
lines.cn: 最佳搭配是与老小、独生子女，或在大家庭中长大的人。

lines.t: The worst match is with another oldest, since the two will be too sovereign to share a household comfortably.
lines.cn: 最差搭配是另一个老大，因为两人都太强势，难以舒服地共处一个家庭。

lines.t: The youngest child of the family thrives on attention, and tends to be outgoing, adventurous, optimistic, creative, and less ambitious than others in the family.
lines.cn: 家里的老小靠关注而成长，往往外向、爱冒险、乐观、有创造力，也比家中其他人更少野心。

lines.t: He may lack self-discipline, and have difficulty making decisions on his own.
lines.cn: 他可能缺乏自律，也难以为自己拿主意。

lines.t: A youngest brother of brothers, often unpredictable and romantic, will match best with an oldest sister of brothers.
lines.cn: 兄弟中的老小，往往难以捉摸而浪漫，最适合与兄弟中的长姐相配。

lines.t: The youngest sister of brothers is best matched with an oldest brother of sisters, who will happily indulge these traits.
lines.cn: 兄弟中的幼妹最适合与姐妹中的长兄相配，后者会乐于纵容她的这些特点。

lines.t: The middle child is influenced by many variables, however, middles are less likely to take initiative, and more anxious and self-critical than others.
lines.cn: 中间的孩子受许多变量影响，不过，中间的孩子不太主动，也比其他人更焦虑、更自我苛责。

lines.t: Middles often successfully marry other middles, since both are strong on tact, not so strong on aggressiveness, and tend to crave affection.
lines.cn: 中间的孩子常常能与另一个中间的孩子幸福结合，因为两人都擅长圆融处世、不那么争强好胜，而且都渴望被爱。

lines.t: The only child is often most comfortable when alone, but since an only tends to be a well-adjusted individual, she'll eventually learn to relate to any chosen spouse.
lines.cn: 独生子女独处时往往最自在，但由于独生子女通常是适应良好的人，她最终会学会与自己选择的配偶相处。

lines.t: The male only child expects his wife to make life easier, without getting much in return.
lines.cn: 男性独生子女指望妻子让生活更轻松，自己却回报不多。

lines.t: He is sometimes best matched with a younger sister of brothers.
lines.cn: 他有时最适合与兄弟中的妹妹相配。

lines.t: The female only child, who tends to be slightly more flexible, is well matched with an older man, who will indulge her tendency to test his love.
lines.cn: 女性独生子女通常稍更灵活，与年长的男性很相配，后者会纵容她考验他爱意的那种倾向。

lines.t: Her worst match?
lines.cn: 她最差的搭配呢？

lines.t: Another only, of course.
lines.cn: 当然是另一个独生子女。
